title: SVD: rotate, stretch, rotate
sub: Any matrix maps the unit circle to an ellipse, in three simple steps.

frames.caption: A = [[2, 1.5], [0.5, 1.2]] acting on the unit circle. The blue and orange arrows are two special perpendicular directions, v₁ and v₂ (the right singular vectors).
Step 1, Vᵀ: rotate so that v₁ and v₂ line up with the axes. A rotation: the circle stays a circle.
Step 2, Σ: stretch along the axes by σ₁ = 2.75 and σ₂ = 0.60. The circle becomes an ellipse whose semi-axes are exactly the singular values.
Step 3, U: rotate the ellipse into place. The arrows now point along u₁ and u₂ (the left singular vectors), with lengths σ₁ and σ₂.
Rotate, stretch, rotate: U Σ Vᵀ = A, exactly. Every matrix does only this to space. Its largest stretch is σ₁, its smallest σ₂, and the ratio σ₁/σ₂ = 4.6 is its condition number.
